title: Update on our Open Desktop AI Art Tool that you can use to craft your game cinematics
author: WiiFitBalanceBoard
selftext:
Hey everyone! I'm part of the team behind ArtCraft - we posted a few weeks back and loved the feedback, so thought we'd come in with an update!

We're still an aggregator of models (Veo, Kling, Flux, Nano Banana, Seedance), and also an aggregator of services (eg. you can log in with Midjourney, and ideally everything) and we're curious to know what would be the most in-demand features! We've added a whole bunch like angle control, image to 3D-World, and are working on an in-suite editor.

It's built in Rust for Desktop. And we'd welcome contributors. I think we can build something better than Freepik, Higgsfield, Krea, etc. and make it totally open source: [https://github.com/storytold/artcraft](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft)

We're not going to try to be Comfy or Invoke - those are local-first tools, which are great, but require a lot of installation and technical capability. We're going to be closer to the commercial foundation models, but an aggregator that is completely yours to own. We also have a bunch of advanced creation modalities like 3D scene layout and blocking that most other tools do not have.

Link: [https://getartcraft.com](https://getartcraft.com)

Join our Discord to track our progress and please let us know what you want to see next!

replies.author: ai_art_is_art
replies.body:
Hi, I'm from the team! 

We've been growing a lot recently, which has been absolutely incredible. The community has been bringing us folks from the gaming and film industry, and it's been exciting. We met Pixar folks, the Russos, it's wild. 

We want to raise capital, but force the VCs to keep 100% of the code open. That sounds weird, but we have a wild idea - we want to build a T-shaped company that turns into an open source hyperscaler. 

Companies like Stability failed because they gave everything away without having a means to generate revenue. ArtCraft is the inverse - we let you purchase credits (or BYOK). We're going to build this into a really solid tool, and we have plans for editing, voice over, music - lots of creative capabilities. (ArtCraft, MusicCraft, etc.) 

The next steps involve infrastructure. OpenFal/OpenOpenRouter - we're close to having this now, but I don't want to launch it since the team is small. But we can effectively do an OpenRouter style overlay that \*also\* supports BYOK and a simple omni-API (unlike Fal's endpoint per model). We can beat them on pricing and companies can feel comfortable that they can bring it all on-prem if they want. 

Phase three would be an OpenRunPod. We'd launch fine tuned models, models with ControlNet support, etc. That'd integrate into our tooling and also be available to API consumers. The goal is that you'll be able to easily launch models with one-click from within ArtCraft, and we're predicting that the open weights models get bigger and better. Eventually competitive with present day models (although that's a moving target). 

If we can do this, we'll have infra in the cloud for running all sorts of open models. We'll then try to build small foundation models in image and voice (we have some experience!), then do more ambitious stuff. 

Once that's done, we have the building blocks for an entire open ecosystem. We think creatives will prefer to have dedicated, special-purpose models that are unconstrained, fine tuneable on a given franchise / brand / style, and that don't fail to generate for arbitrary rules. 

And from there maybe we can get into running coding models and tools... who knows. I'd like to build an open ecosystem of tools and infra though. We just also need good default rails to get paid (like Valve with Steam) so we can grow and fund this venture. 

By being ridiculously open, we kind of make it stupid hard to compete if you're a website aggregator. 

We'll see - it's a big plan. I have a few interested VCs from good firms asking to meet, but we need a little bit more traction. We're pretty far along - 100,000x January numbers (which were basically nil), but every subscription helps.
